meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
I know who you are, Hale. Why did my son find out from his phone?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. And the zero itself, on what basis?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
Eleven thirty-one, eleven fifty-two, eleven fifty-eight; I'm writing that down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, and people paste from somewhere else all the time. Turn the screen.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up. And before you entered anything, did you ask Owen where those words came from?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
A seventeen-year-old misquoting Shakespeare is a bad mark, Hale, not proof of anything. You skipped my question. Did you speak to Owen first?
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their argument after an outline; that's what an outline is for. And you've stepped around my question twice, so I'll take that as a no.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
Fine, you spoke to him; a tired kid put on the spot by a teacher he says has had it in for him since September. Is anything on his record right now, Hale?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a take-home essay is no comparison. Answer me. His record.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good, because the company that sells it says not to use it alone. And you've ducked his record twice, which tells me I'm going to the principal today.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4, and I'll take it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Private, not in front of his class, marked before December 1, and nothing on his record, in writing tonight. When?
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Yes, if it's marked before December 1, and you still haven't told me when. Ten minutes, Hale.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday the twelfth, after school. And the promise about his record in my inbox tonight.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Yes, on Thursday after school, and marked well before December 1.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
Who else has seen this?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

You agreed today that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite of his Hamlet essay on Thursday after school, that its mark will replace the zero and be in well before December 1, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still require that promise in writing, and I still want to know who else has seen this concern. I expect your written confirmation tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and accepted a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school, marked before December 1, with nothing on his record; she still wants your written promise tonight and to know who else has seen the concern, and that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her call cut it off.
What moved her: Your dated note from November 2 showing you had spoken with Owen before entering the zero, because it answered a procedural point she had been pressing and left her nothing left to argue on process.
What cost ground: Leaving her questions about whether you spoke to Owen and whether anything was on his record unanswered for several turns, because each dodge pushed her toward the principal and kept her hostile.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history showing the essay appearing between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, landed squarely on that kind of late night, which proves nothing about the essay but is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anything was on his record, tell her right away that nothing is and that procedure 4.4 keeps it that way, before showing your next document.
